Trenchers — common questions

What is a trencher used for?

Trenchers cut narrow channels in the ground for underground utilities — water and sewer pipes, electrical and fiber cable, gas lines, drainage tile, irrigation lines, landscape lighting and invisible fence.

Trencher vs excavator — which is better for utility lines?

A trencher is faster and cleaner for any long, narrow, uniform channel. An excavator is better when you need wider trenches, deeper digs, or have obstacles that require a bucket. Many contractors run both.

How deep can a Konstructz trencher dig?

The GROUP RIPPER GRX is designed to dig trenches up to 48 inches deep and 6 inches wide using a standard heavy-duty chain. Confirm your required depth and chain width with Konstructz to select the best setup.

What soils does a trencher handle?

With the correct tooth pattern, a trencher cuts through topsoil, clay, packed dirt, shale and roots. Solid rock and large boulders are not a trencher application — those need a rock saw or breaker.
